summary: EarthPulse is an interactive map that lets people explore Earth’s weather through sound as well as sight. Users select locations and hear live weather data translated into a layered soundscape: temperature controls the root pitch, humidity shapes harmonic richness, and wind drives rhythmic pulses and atmospheric texture. Sound-layer controls, location comparisons, explanatory readouts, and Acoustic GeoGuessr invite users to isolate patterns, compare places, and learn how environmental data shapes what they hear. We could not access NASA EIC visualization frames during development, so this prototype uses live weather data rather than claiming direct sonification of EIC imagery. EarthPulse demonstrates an exploratory approach to making Earth science perceivable through sound, and provides a foundation for integrating EIC visualizations or datasets when available.
details:
EarthPulse is an interactive map that turns weather conditions into sound, giving people another way to explore how environments differ around the world. Users can search for a place or select one on the map, view its weather, and listen to a soundscape generated from its temperature, humidity, and wind speed.

The sound is built from three data mappings: temperature controls the root pitch, humidity shapes harmonic richness, and wind speed drives rhythmic pulses and atmospheric texture. The map’s sound-wave visualizer responds while audio plays. Users can experiment with the mappings in the Sonification Lab, compare locations, and play Acoustic GeoGuessr, which asks them to identify a hidden location by listening and placing a map pin. After locking in, they see the result and an explanation of how the weather values shaped the sound.

The project’s intended impact is to make environmental data more engaging and perceivable through both sight and sound. It may support learning for people who prefer auditory exploration, though it is a prototype—not a substitute for a fully tested accessibility tool.

We developed EarthPulse with React, TypeScript, and Next.js. D3-Geo powers the interactive map, while Tone.js and the Web Audio API generate the soundscapes. Weather data is retrieved through the application’s weather API. No special hardware is required; the experience runs in a web browser with speakers or headphones.

The creative element is treating weather as a musical system rather than simply reading values aloud. We designed the mappings to make different environmental conditions audible while keeping the result musical and adjustable. During development, we considered clarity of the data-to-sound mappings, user control, and avoiding answer reveals before a game guess is locked in.

Data limitation: We could not access NASA EIC visualization frames during development. EarthPulse currently sonifies weather data; it does not analyze or directly sonify NASA EIC imagery. We see this as a foundation for integrating EIC data or visualizations when accessible.
